bites.title: Email consent and unsubscribe rules (e.g., CASL in Canada)
bites.body:
Anti-spam laws such as Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL), UK PECR, and GDPR govern when a business may send commercial electronic messages and require a clear, working unsubscribe mechanism in every email. Because legal rules and penalties carry strict enforcement, check the current details for every country your client targets.

It is like knocking on doors in a neighbourhood where local bylaws forbid cold-calling at houses without an invitation; ignoring the sign on the gate brings heavy fines, not customers.

Never build an agent that scrapes personal email addresses off the web and blasts unsolicited campaigns without verifying legal consent status in the CRM first.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · fast-moving topic, check current details · confidence: medium

questions.prompt: What must an automated email marketing workflow verify before sending a commercial message to a contact?

choices.text: That the email contains at least four different font colours and an animated attachment
That the message is sent at 3:00 am so spam filters are asleep
That valid consent exists for that recipient's jurisdiction and that a working unsubscribe link is included
That the unsubscribe link is hidden in white text on a white background

questions.explanation: Respecting recorded consent flags and providing effortless opt-outs protects the client from severe regulatory penalties and domain blacklisting.

bites.title: Advertising platform policies
bites.body:
Every major advertising network enforces strict automated policies covering prohibited products, personal-attribute targeting phrasing, landing page quality, and substantiation of claims. Because ad networks revise their enforcement algorithms frequently, check the current details before launching an automated ad workflow.

It is like shipping freight through an international customs port; even if your cargo is legal in your home town, violating the port authority's manifest rules will get your entire container impounded.

Repeated policy violations caused by an unmonitored ad-copy agent do not just get single ads rejected; they can get the client's entire advertising account permanently suspended right before their peak trading season.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · fast-moving topic, check current details · confidence: medium

questions.prompt: What is the biggest business risk of letting an agent submit paid ads without checking advertising platform policies?

choices.text: The advertising platform will accidentally transfer money into the client's bank account
Ad platforms charge a lower cost per click whenever an ad violates their rules
Rejected ads automatically get published on the front page of national newspapers
Repeated automated policy violations can trigger a permanent suspension of the client's entire ad account

questions.explanation: Ad platforms penalise accounts that repeatedly submit non-compliant creatives, making pre-submission policy checks essential.

bites.title: Disclose AI-generated content where required
bites.body:
Platform terms, industry codes, and emerging regulations increasingly require advertisers and publishers to label realistic AI-generated images, audio, or video so audiences are not misled by synthetic media. Because disclosure rules vary by platform and jurisdiction, check the current details for each channel your client uses.

Think of food packaging rules that require a drink made with artificial flavouring to say so clearly on the label rather than claiming it was squeezed from fresh orchard fruit.

Help clients set a clear policy: disclose synthetic media transparently where required, and never use AI voice or face clones of real people without explicit written permission.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · fast-moving topic, check current details · confidence: medium

questions.prompt: When a marketing team uses realistic AI-generated video or audio in a campaign, why must they check disclosure requirements?

choices.text: Labelling a video as AI-generated automatically doubles its organic search ranking on every platform
Disclosure rules only apply to black-and-white photographs taken before 1950
Audio files cannot play on mobile phones unless a disclosure tag is embedded in the filename
Platforms and laws increasingly mandate clear labelling of realistic synthetic media so audiences are not deceived

questions.explanation: Checking and following synthetic-media disclosure rules protects the brand from platform takedowns, legal breaches, and audience backlash.

bites.title: Never invent testimonials, reviews, or results
bites.body:
An agentic marketing system must never fabricate customer quotes, invent five-star reviews, or make up case study percentages. Fake social proof is both unethical and illegal under consumer protection laws across the UK, Canada, the EU, and the US.

It is like a restaurant proprietor writing fake hygiene certificates and fictional critic reviews on the menu; the moment a diner or inspector checks, the restaurant's reputation and licence are ruined.

Configure copywriting prompts and reviewer checklists with a hard ban on placeholder testimonials. Even writing a "sample quote to be replaced later" is dangerous because busy staff sometimes publish drafts without noticing the fake quote.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: Why should copywriting agents be forbidden from generating even placeholder customer testimonials in drafts?

choices.text: Customer testimonials are never effective at persuading B2B buyers
Language models cannot use quotation marks without crashing the server
Busy reviewers can easily miss a realistic-looking placeholder quote and accidentally publish illegal fake reviews
Real customers are legally barred from praising a product in writing

questions.explanation: Banning fabricated quotes and statistics even at the draft stage prevents accidental publication of deceptive social proof.

bites.title: Approval for anything that makes a claim about price or outcomes
bites.body:
Every marketing asset that states a price, discount terms, warranty promise, or measurable customer outcome must pass through a documented human approval gate before going live. Models can easily miscombine two different offers into an unintended promise.

Imagine a car dealership assistant accidentally printing a poster offering a five-year free servicing package on clearance vans where margins are already razor-thin; customers who turn up with the poster will rightly expect the deal to be honoured.

Have your reviewer agent highlight every number, percentage, currency symbol, and guarantee phrase in a draft so the human approver can verify each claim against the current offer sheet in seconds.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: Why should a workflow automatically highlight every price, percentage, and outcome claim for human approval before publishing?

choices.text: Marketing materials are never allowed to mention prices or numbers in any industry
Highlighting numbers automatically converts pounds into foreign currencies without checking exchange rates
Human approvers only care about punctuation and never check commercial figures
Unverified pricing or outcome promises create binding commercial and legal obligations if an agent misstates the offer

questions.explanation: Surfacing every commercial number and outcome claim ensures a human verifies the exact offer terms before the public sees them.
